design: Tier 1, no migration. D1 (wpc3-c). Track the newest help (the service's list), not the Hub's pinned build; the drift script prints the build it compared against. D2 (wpc3-b). Stored values outlive the catalog: the trigger accepts an override equal to the conversation's stored model, as runners.py already tolerates a runner's current model. D3 (wpc3-f). Validate on write, tolerate at run: run_worker no longer refuses an undeclared model (every worker model is a stored one); writes that choose one (runner, manager job PATCH since F630, checkpoint_model newly set) refuse it. Copilot then runs it or substitutes silently, which the session-start change will report.

checked: worker.run_worker returns unknown_model for an undeclared model
limits: No Copilot turn is driven at home; the work-PC drive covers a live session

problem: On the work-PC drive (Copilot CLI 1.0.94-3) a trigger override with claude-haiku-5.5 was refused 400 though the CLI runs it, and grok-4.7 likewise, while four retired models (claude-opus-4.7, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.5-flash, kimi-k2.7-code) were still offered. The pinning test stayed green because its fixture is 1.0.90. Refreshing alone would break what is stored: a conversation's runtime_overrides on a removed model would be refused on every operator message, and one-shot workers (checkpoints, distillation, vault jobs) refuse any undeclared model outright (worker.py), so background work would stop.

requirements.rationale: The model list is the service's; every model the Hub's older build offers live is in the newest help (wpc3-c).
requirements.statement: CATALOG['copilot'] MUST declare exactly the model ids of copilot help config 1.0.94-3, in that build's order after auto, and its pinning test MUST compare against that build's captured help text.

requirements.rationale: A refresh must not stop work already configured (wpc3-b, wpc3-f).
requirements.statement: A model the catalog no longer declares MUST keep working where it is already stored: a trigger override equal to the conversation's stored model is accepted, and a one-shot worker runs a stored model with a logged warning instead of refusing it as unknown_model; a newly chosen undeclared model (a different override, a runner, a manager job, or a newly set checkpoint_model) MUST still be refused naming the catalog.

requirements.rationale: The runner already says '— unrecognised'; a conversation must not present a removed model as current.
requirements.statement: A conversation's response MUST carry model_unrecognised, true when its stored runtime_overrides model is one its runner's catalog does not declare.

in_scope: model_catalog: _COPILOT_MODEL_IDS = copilot help config 1.0.94-3, in its order; the pinning fixture follows
scripts/check_model_catalog.py prints the build it compared against
validate_overrides tolerates a model equal to the one already stored on the conversation
run_worker runs a stored model the catalog no longer declares, with a warning, instead of refusing it
project settings validate a newly set checkpoint_model against the runner's catalog (manager jobs: F630)
non_goals: Reporting a model Copilot substituted at session start (its own change)
Per-model effort values (its own change, with the substitution report)
The composer pill's 'unrecognised' label (UI batch; the flag is here)

summary: CATALOG['copilot'] becomes the 30 models of copilot help config 1.0.94-3; a model that leaves the catalog keeps working where it is already stored, flagged, and is refused only when newly chosen (F662, decision fix-D5).
